Selling brushes and other digital assets sounds simple… until you realize that making the asset is only half the job! After 1,000+ sales, I’ve learned a LOT about what actually makes people click “buy,” what makes them come back, and what turns a good digital product into a great one! Here are the biggest lessons I wish I knew when I started: ★ Make something you’d actually use yourself! Never sell any product you wouldn’t personally endorse, all the brushes I sell are brushes I actively use in my own art. If you want people to trust your product, set a good example! My artwork actively advertises all of my brushes because when people like my art and want to recreate it themselves, I can point them to my shop!  ★ Presentation matters almost as much as the product. Your previews need to sell the result, not just show the files! A good listing that not only catches the eye, but actively shows people what they’ll be buying increasing your chances of someone purchasing your product! My listings show off the brush, the title of the brush, what it can be used for, and some of my artwork using that brush! People don’t read descriptions, put valuable information in your product listings.   ★ Making a product is only half the battle. Advertising is more important because the best product will fail if no one knows it exists or understands why they need to buy it! Find your niche and learn how to reach your audience, a lot of artists would really benefit from learning a thing or two about marketing & branding especially if they want to make a career out of selling.  ★ A great customer experience is part of the product. Anybody can make a brush, but people are choosing to buy from YOU, make it an experience worth while! People who have a good experience purchasing from you are more likely to come back and customer retention/loyalty is so important! Also, your customers are the BEST use of free advertising! If they like the product, they might recommend it to their friends, driving more sales to your shop without any extra hassle :)  ★ You don’t need thousands of followers to make digital assets worth selling. A lot of my followers actually came AFTER I started selling my work!  1,000 sales later, I’m still learning, but these are the things I’d focus on if I were starting from zero today :3 If you’re an artist thinking about selling your own brushes/assets on VGen, save this for later!  · · ─ ·ʚɞ· ─ · ·  ⊹ ࣪ ˖ ໒꒱ Materials Used: ★ XPPen Artist 16 3rd Pro ★ iPad Pro M4 + Apple Pencil 2nd Gen ★ Clip Studio Paint Want my brushes? — ᨳଓ . Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.  That's what I love about learning skills that can create income from home. I'm not looking for another job. I'm building more ways to earn—and more choices for my future. Financial freedom doesn't have to start with something huge. It can start with one product that solves one problem.
